newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates linger with only call up.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates linger with only call up.

text.p: Most Dutch money market rates were unchanged on Friday as market players held back, awaiting U.S. economic data due later in the afternoon.
Dealers said trade focused on short-term deposits of one week to one month, while call also saw moderate activity.
Overnight money was bid between 3.06 and 3.12 percent, six basis points higher than on Thursday.

Dealers said call rates were driven higher by a relatively tight allocation under the special advances pact this morning, with additional upward pressure caused by demand from the Finance Ministry's Agency.
Call changed hands at up to 3.125 percent, they said.
This morning, the Dutch central bank allocated 2.91 billion guilders to the money market under a seven-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent.
Individual banks' applications up to 3.50 billion guilders were met for 11.5 percent. Above that level no subscriptions were awarded.
The pact replaced an eight-day facility of 3.05 billion guilders which expired today.
The guilder traded virtually unchanged versus the mark, at 112.5125 per 100 marks versus 112.5025 on Thursday.
